summary: Recent election results have energized D.C. statehood advocates, who say the political landscape has shifted in their favor. Meanwhile, D.C. residents continue to navigate local governance challenges—including disputes over utility reforms, Medicaid coverage, and Council succession—while facing federal legal conflicts over matters like the proposed Triumphal Arch and concerns about federal interference in local affairs. Without statehood, D.C. residents have no senators, and their one delegate to the House cannot vote on the House floor.
